text: Day had broken cold and gray. <break time="0.8s" /> When the man turned off the main Yukon trail. <break time="0.8s" /> And climbed the high bank. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the frozen river. <break time="0.8s" /> It was nine oclock. <break time="0.8s" /> But there was no sun or hint of sun. <break time="0.8s" /> And a strange gloom lay. <break time="0.8s" /> Over the white land. <break time="0.8s" /> The strangeness of it all. <break time="0.8s" /> Made no impression on the man. <break time="0.8s" /> A newcomer in the land. <break time="0.8s" /> For this was his first winter there. <break time="0.8s" /> Fifty degrees below zero. <break time="0.8s" /> Meant eighty odd degrees of frost to him. <break time="0.8s" /> And that fact seemed. <break time="0.8s" /> Only cold and uncomfortable. <break time="0.8s" /> The trouble with him was that he had no imagination. <break time="0.8s" /> So the cold never made him think. <break time="0.8s" /> About his own weakness as a human. <break time="0.8s" /> To test the cold. <break time="0.8s" /> He spat. <break time="0.8s" /> And the spit crackled sharply in the air. <break time="0.8s" /> Before it could fall to the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> He knew that spit crackled on the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> At fifty below. <break time="0.8s" /> So it was surely colder than that but how much colder. <break time="0.8s" /> He did not know. <break time="0.8s" /> He was heading for an old claim. <break time="0.8s" /> On Henderson Creek. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the boys were already waiting. <break time="0.8s" /> And he would be there. <break time="0.8s" /> By six oclock. <break time="0.8s" /> His lunch of biscuits. <break time="0.8s" /> Was wrapped in a handkerchief. <break time="0.8s" /> And carried inside his shirt. <break time="0.8s" /> Against his bare skin. <break time="0.8s" /> To keep it from freezing.
